fields.v: Squeez-2B (Qwen 3.5 2B + LoRA; no version). Compared with zero-shot Qwen 3.5 35B A3B, Kimi K2, Qwen 3.5 2B base, and heuristics BM25, First-N, Last-N, Random (each keeping ~10% of lines)
None of the SDD kind. Input: focused extraction query + one raw tool observation; output: verbatim relevant lines wrapped in <relevant lines> tags (gold: line spans). Not specifications

Not a development flow. Pruning step inserted between a tool call and the agent's next reasoning step (vLLM-served model or CLI filter on piped output). Dataset pipeline: collect tool outputs, teacher LLM writes query and selects spans, manual curation of test set, LoRA fine-tuning
None in the pruning flow; manual curation of the held-out test set (111 of 729 candidates excluded)
Single component evaluated offline on single tool observations; no coding agent or full trajectory run
Not classifiable (context pruning for agents, no specification); author uses no SDD terms
Existing code bases (tool outputs from SWE-bench repository snapshots) plus synthetic tool outputs; offline pruning task, not issue resolution

11,477 examples (9,205 SWE-derived, 1,697 synthetic positives, 575 synthetic negatives), 27 tool types; split 10,508 train / 240 dev / 618 test; average input tokens per tool family 60 (python) to 3,418 (type check)
Coding-agent tool outputs: Python repositories from SWE-bench (file reads, grep, git, tests, linters, pip, curl) and synthetic TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, Docker, Terraform, Kubernetes outputs
N/A (no participants)
Compression (fraction of input lines/tokens removed). No latency, tokens of a downstream agent or money; training on one NVIDIA A100 80GB
Line-level precision, recall, tolerant F1 (fuzzy substring similarity >0.5), strict exact-text F1, exact match against gold spans; empty-output rate on negatives
None
None
Qualitative error patterns (Table 5); recall-compression trade-off (Fig. 2)
Automatic line matching of predictions against gold spans; gold spans produced by teacher LLM (openai/gpt-oss-120b); test set manually reviewed by the author

618-example held-out test set; no coding agent run (offline pruning of single tool observations). Success criterion: none stated by the authors (metrics compared against LLM-generated, manually curated gold spans). Values: precision; recall; strict F1; exact; F1 (tolerant); compression. rev.why: The authors state no success criterion (no threshold on recall, F1 or compression), so the works/partly/does-not-work verdicts were the extractor's own and are removed (author's rule of 2026-11-23). Metric values re-checked against Table 4 and text p. 5: unchanged.

fields.v: Held-out 618-example test set (split by repository / tool family). Configurations: Squeez-2B vs 3 zero-shot LLMs and 4 heuristics. Baseline: Qwen 3.5 2B base and heuristics. Held constant: same <query>/<tool output> prompt for all generative models; heuristics at ~10% of lines. Acceptance: gold spans. Repetitions: not stated (single run). Human intervention: N/A

Squeez-2B best on precision, recall and F1: recall +11 pts vs Qwen 3.5 35B A3B (0.86 vs 0.75) and +33 vs 2B base, at the same 92% compression; heuristics far lower (BM25 recall 0.22). Negatives: 80% vs 7% (Qwen 35B) correct empty output. No significance test

Distinguished all systems clearly. Repeatability: single run, no variance reported. Limitations stated: single observations not trajectories; span overlap misses valid alternative prunings; grep and lint labels noisier
No downstream end-to-end task-completion evaluation; usefulness approximated by span overlap; noisier tool families (grep, lint); residual errors are adjacent over-selection

Table 4 (p. 4) and Table 5 (p. 5) jumbled by pdftotext; Table 4 rebuilt by column order (rows Squeez-2B, Qwen 35B, Kimi K2, Qwen 2B base, BM25, First-N, Random, Last-N) and checked against text p. 4 (11 and 33 recall points, BM25 0.22). Gold labels are LLM-generated (gpt-oss-120b), test set manually curated. Model, dataset, evaluation code and CLI released (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/KRLabsOrg/squeez and Hugging Face. Abstract says "92% of input tokens" while compression is defined as fraction of input removed (line unit). Split counts 10,508 + 240 + 618 = 11,366, not the 11,477 released examples; the difference equals the 111 test candidates excluded in curation (10,508 + 240 + 729 = 11,477), so the total apparently still counts them (p. 3). No pre-registration. Language: Python (SWE-bench) plus synthetic multi-ecosystem

rev.why: A reporting inconsistency was missing: the train/dev/test split (p. 3) does not add up to the stated benchmark total of 11,477.
